# 1.2.92 - the contract with Foundry and Daggerheart: what the module relies on is checked at start, a stable macro API, one diagnostics report, and a named data migration

Stage E52 ships with this version, alone. At each load the primary GM's browser now reads every place where the module
relies on code that is not its own (Foundry's, Daggerheart's, other modules'). A place that is not as this version expects
is told to the GMs in one notice that stays until closed and in a Pre-season checks line, each with what the table gets
instead. `game.drpg.diagnose()` is one report to copy, the macro API has a written surface that a test holds the code to,
and the data migration has its own name, `game.drpg.migrate()`. 13 commits on 1.2.91 (4616d1d1), up to 2709fe03, the last
before the release commit. What was counted and what was not is in Known gaps and Checked.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **What changes in a running world.** No migration is added and no setting is added. `migrate.mjs` changes its header and
   its log line only (the log now says "the data migration"). One thing is removed from a browser: at start,
   `recommendsSilenced`, a client value of the recommended-modules window (gone since E13 C10, read by no code), is
   deleted from that browser's storage, and the report names it. `module.json` has no diff from 1.2.91. No bridge
   row, socket event or GM store is added (`gm-bridge.mjs` and `gm-stores.mjs` are not among the changed files, and the stage
   adds no row a player's browser sends). `game.drpg` gains `diagnose`, `migrate` and `trialVoice`; every name it had stays
   (the alias table is in For the GM). `lang/en.json` goes from 4277 strings to 4355 (78 added, none removed, 2 reworded:
   `DRPG.Requirements.newerSystemPatches` and `newerSystemAllPatches`) and `lang/pl.json` from 5122 to 5208 (86 added, none
   removed, 2 reworded), counted with node on both files at 4616d1d1 and at HEAD. `tools/api-surface.json` is the one new
   file.
3. **The owner's answers.** E52, of 30.10:
   - **1a, Levels.** A region whose Foundry level check fails (the check itself throws an error) is read on the floors it
     lists, not on every floor, as a region without that check already is. The first plan read it as "on every floor"; that
     is changed. For a table: each region is drawn on its own floors and nothing goes black, and a token on one floor is not
     judged to stand in another floor's room.
   - **2a, the old API names.** They stay as aliases, with no release set for removing them (`migrate1_2_0` is listed as kept
     until 1.3.1, and the other eight have no end date). A macro written with an old name keeps working.
   - **3a, the microphone block.** In a Foundry that does not name the user permission `BROADCAST_AUDIO`, the block writes
     nothing and the GM is told why (the voice list: "This version of Foundry has no microphone permission, so no microphone
     can be blocked from here."). Nobody's microphone is blocked in that case.
   - **4a, the Polish texts.** The owner read the Polish contract texts on a page made for the phone and approved them as
     they are for this stage ("Na ten etap jest w porzadku"); a general review of the texts (E65, E66, E71) will take them
     later. A read of them at the table is still open.
   - **5, default.** The texts of decisions D24 and D25 were not known to the stage. Its reading stays: a failed check gives
     the fallback each file already had, the rolls keep their own fallback and nothing is loosened, and a name leaves the
     macro API only after staying as an alias for at least one release. This note does not claim to quote D24 or D25.

## At the table

### For the GM

- **A notice when something the module relies on is not as expected.** One notice per load, kept until you close it, names
  each such place with its file and function and what the table gets instead; a place found failing later in the same load (the
  first character sheet drawn, a scene with floors opened later) gets a notice of its own, and no place is named twice in a
  load. Nothing is written to the world. The rows that guard trust (the guard on Daggerheart's GM relay, the roll draw, what a
  player may read of a roll) keep their own fallbacks and words, and a failed one is never turned into a looser one. A row
  checks presence, not behaviour; a place nothing here could read is "unknown", a warning and never a pass.
- **Pre-season checks** show the same rows: each failed place on its own line with a cross, the places nobody could check
  as one counted line with the list folded under it ("{n} places could not be checked here, so they are not known to work."),
  a tick only when every place holds. GM handbook, section 20, "The contract with Foundry, Daggerheart and the modules", lists
  all 59 fallbacks in words; some of them: a failed `door-controls` leaves every door control as Foundry shows it,
  `roll-draw` throws rolls in the player's own browser as in 1.2.66, `chat-content-visible` leaves the player who rolled
  unable to read a roll the GM drew, `sheet-anchors` leaves what the module adds at a missing sheet place undrawn and the rest
  of the sheet as usual.
- **Doors.** A Foundry door-control class whose chain has no `isVisible` is left as Foundry's, so doors open, and the row is
  named as failed. Read on the harness's model, not on a canvas (B-E52-5).
- **The report.** `game.drpg.diagnose()` opens a window with everything this browser can check as one text, returns the same
  text, and **Copy report** puts it on the clipboard. It has 21 parts, the contract first and then the data migration, the
  failures since the page loaded, the silenced warnings, and the existing `diagnose...()` parts (Dice to Traps). On a
  player's browser the eight parts that read what only GMs know are named and say "GM only"; none of their data is in a
  player's report. The window lists the silenced warnings by id with **Show again**; the one the module keeps is the
  Daggerheart-is-newer warning, silenced per version.
- **The page-tint notice** now appears only for a named Dark Reader; a big unnamed inline sheet is a console line and a line in
  the Styles part. The Styles and Windows parts read the theme's own fonts, the style-file pattern for css and woff2 with a
  query, and `traceClicks` hears a click cancelled on its way back up.
- **Macros.** `game.drpg.migrate()` is the data migration (`migrate({ force: true })` runs it whether or not the version
  moved); `migrate1_2_0` is the same function. An actor argument that is no id and no name now warns with the call and the word
  given instead of doing nothing; a name two actors share warns and acts on the first, as before. `traitValue` works when
  destructured. `trialVoice` is on `game.drpg`. Aliases kept: `migrate1_2_0` to `migrate`, `advanceFloorNow` to `skipStep`,
  `extendFloor` to `adjustTime`, `endFloor` to `endMode`, `exportLedger` to `backupCase`, `importLedger` to `restoreCase`,
  `isSilenced` to `isCrimeSilenced`, `musicDialog` to `soundDialog`, `currentRoom` to `roomOfActor`.
  `tools/api-surface.json` lists 450 keys of `game.drpg` and a test holds the live object to it.
- **Microphone block without the permission:** see answer 3a above.

### For players

- **Nothing is added to what a player's browser sends**, and the contract is read on the primary GM's browser. A player sees
  what a failed row's fallback shows (for example doors drawn by Foundry), not the notice.
- **A player's own report** (`game.drpg.diagnose()` in their console) holds the parts their browser may read and names the
  eight GM-only parts without running them. Measured by a stand-in player on the GM's client, not on a real player's browser.
- **Regions and floors:** answer 1a, above. A player is shown each region on the floors it lists.

### For everybody

- **The contract writes nothing to the world.** A client's memory and the GM's notice only.
- **The Polish and English texts of the notice, the Pre-season lines and the report are paired** (parity and prose checks
  green on the lang files; the figures are in Before installing). Console lines stay English.

## Known gaps

- **E52-11, partial.** Presence probes only where Foundry exposes the name; the rest are "unknown" with a table row. The
  Foundry icon file `icons/fvtt.png` has no row. **E52-12, partial:** `SHEET_ANCHORS` holds 18 places, not the 25 or so of the
  plan; places the sheet code only removes are left out; three places the code does without are optional.
- **The registry's reading.** R1537 reads literal hook names and misses an override reached through a parameter declared
  elsewhere. R1549 reads with comments blanked, because the test kit's `stripComments` blanks real code in `sheet.mjs`
  `tidySidebar`. R1551 stands a player in on the GM's client. R1560 leaves `suiteRolling` out by name and is skipped on a
  table installed without `tools/`. The page-tint fix (E52-17) has no permanent test; a scratch run with a 250-rule unnamed
  sheet failed before and passed after.
- **Wording not final.** Unknown rows' notes stay English inside Pre-season's Polish window and the console. The text of the
  B-E52-1 live row quotes 9 unknown rows from C2; a correctness probe at 03e73d82 read 60 rows on the GM, 0 failed and 30
  unknown, and the row is to be refreshed.
- **The eclipse values.** `ECLIPSE_FREE_PLACEMENT` is still `["night"]` and `eclipseMovesLeft` may answer null at night
  (E37 has not shipped); the surface file says so.
- **`trialVoice`.** On a player's browser it answers "muted" for a death nobody has found, read from the world setting
  `trialProgress`; this is the known item TR30, to be closed with E67.
- **D24 and D25.** Their text was not in the sources; see answer 5.
- **Not measured at HEAD:** CI, the whole suite, all scenarios and tier 2. CI at 03e73d82 is not stated in the stage's
  records.
